text: From the oval shaped flower bed there rose perhaps a hundred stalks, spreading into heart shaped or tongue shaped leaves half way up and unfurling at the tip red or blue or yellow petals marked with spots of color raised upon the surface. <break time="0.8s" /> Out of the dim throat of each flower emerged a straight bar, rough with gold dust and slightly clubbed at the end, and the petals were voluminous enough to be stirred by the summer breeze. <break time="0.8s" /> When the petals moved, the red, blue, and yellow lights passed one over the other, staining an inch of the brown earth beneath with a spot of the most intricate color. <break time="0.8s" /> The light fell upon the smooth gray back of a pebble or the shell of a snail, or, falling into a raindrop, it expanded with such intense color that one expected the drop to burst. <break time="0.8s" /> Men and women walked past the flower bed with a curiously irregular movement, not unlike that of the white and blue butterflies that crossed the turf in zigzag flights from bed to bed. <break time="0.8s" /> A married couple with two children came by, the man strolling carelessly about six inches in front of the woman, who now and then turned her head to see that the children were not too far behind. <break time="0.8s" /> The man, whose name was Simon, kept this distance on purpose, though perhaps unconsciously, for he wanted to go on with his thoughts, which had been carried back fifteen years to this very garden.
